Cross-referencing the statement with insights from the Financial Stability Report, the macro tone remains cautiously positive: labor markets are strong, inflation is near the symmetric 2 percent objective, and the Committee signals gradual normalization from an accommodative stance. However, the FSR’s emphasis on elevated asset valuations, rising nonfinancial business leverage (notably in riskier credit), and pockets of vulnerability in asset markets—offset by solid bank capital/liquidity and contained funding risks—tempers the outlook. These stability considerations support gradualism and the “balanced risks” framing rather than an exuberant stance. Net: modestly positive, but constrained by financial-stability vulnerabilities.
